notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Declan Carlile has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 86:15 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 49% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:06 together.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Penguins (7-10-2) beat San Jose 3-2 in a shootout on Nov 11, and the Blues have won two in a row. Going in, the Blues are seventh in the Central (tied for 18th in the NHL) and the Pens sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th).

The Blues’ record (.526) is about what their chances are worth. The Penguins have played better than their record (.421) says: their chances are worth about .548, and their finishing has held them back.

The Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). The Penguins rarely throw hits (lowest) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), so the Blues have the edge over them on forecheck pressure. The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Blues.

Jimmy Snuggerud (10 G / 4 A / 14 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Blues’ scoring lead. Robert Thomas (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 19 GP) shares it, with a point in five straight games against Pittsburgh. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 19 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Joel Hofer (8-5-1 / .926 SV% in 14 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start. Pittsburgh has two options in net: Artūrs Šilovs (5-6-1 / .873 SV% in 12 GS) and Sergei Murashov (2-4-1 / .891 SV% in 7 GS). Šilovs has started seven of their last ten games, so expect him back in net after Murashov got the last one on Nov 11.
